newsitem.title: MEXICO: Raul Salinas's lawyer denies client's drug ties.
newsitem.headline: Raul Salinas's lawyer denies client's drug ties.

text.p: Raul Salinas's lawyer denied a report on Thursday that the ex-president's brother received millions of dollars in cash from a Mexican drug cartel and stashed the money in a secret Swiss bank account.

The Miami Herald reported that Swiss authorities believe at least $100 million in Salinas's bank account in Switzerland was the product of payoffs by a leading drug lord during Carlos Salinas's 1988-1994 term.

Switzerland has been investigating Raul Salinas ever since an $84 million secret bank account was discovered and its assets frozen in late 1995. Several more of Salinas's accounts were discovered later in Switzerland and elsewhere.

Eduardo Luengo Creel, one of Salinas's main lawyers, told reporters in Mexico City that his client's Swiss money was not linked to drugs and was instead from a trust fund that belonged to several prominent Mexican industrialists.
"It is clear some authorities are more interested in keeping the money than proving its true source," Luengo said.
The Swiss government can seize the money legally if it proves it was laundered, according to Luengo.
Raul Salinas is in a maximum-security jail near Mexico City on charges of murder and illicit enrichment. Last week, Mexico also brought money-laundering charges against him.

Luengo said much of the money in the account belonged to Mexican business tycoons, including telecommunications magnate Carlos Peralta and Roberto Gonzalez, the founder and head of tortilla firm Grupo Industrial Maseca SA.
"It's money from Carlos Peralta and Roberto Gonzalez, who are industrialists of international reknown and have the financial capacity to make investments of this magnitude," Luengo said.

It was the first time Salinas or his lawyers had said that Gonzalez, a godfather of Carlos Salinas and one of Mexico's richest men, gave money to the alleged trust fund. In early 1996, Peralta suggested Gonzalez had participated in the fund, something vehemently denied by Gonzalez at the time.
Eduardo Sastre, a spokesman for Maseca, told Reuters on Thursday that Gonzalez never participated in an investment fund with Raul Salinas.

Peralta admitted in early 1996 that he gave $50 million to Raul Salinas, a revelation that sparked charges by Mexico's opposition that the businessmen had bribed Raul during his brothers' administration in return for government favours.

But Swiss authorities are convinced the money came in large part from drug traffickers like Juan Garcia Abrego, the former head of the powerful Gulf cartel who was arrested last year in Mexico and has been on trial in the United States, according to the Herald.

"We are more convinced than when we started the case that this money is drug money," the newspaper quoted Valentin Roschacher, Switzerland's top anti-drug official, as saying to the PBS television's Frontline in a soon-to-be aired programme.
